title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
authors: Xi He, Chao Zhang, Shilin Huang, Bei Zeng
abstract: We establish that transversal diagonal gates on exact qubit codes of distance at least two can be exhaustively classified within a finite search space. Although code-preserving physical gates can have continuous phases, any projective logical action induced by a transversal diagonal gate can always be realized by a physical gate of finite order. Crucially, we prove that this physical order has an upper bound determined solely by the code parameters. This order bound enables the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework introduced in arXiv:2504.20847 to exhaustively enumerate all candidate discrete symmetries, after which the Knill-Laflamme equations determine the remaining continuous code parameters. Applying this method to the nontrivial diagonal sector of exact $((6,2,3))$ codes, SSLP yields $66$ candidate symmetry classes, of which exactly $15$ are realizable, supporting full projective diagonal logical cyclic groups of orders $2$, $3$, and $5$. In particular, for order $5$, the code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations, equivalent to the code constructed in arXiv:2504.20847. This code also attains the minimum length $n=6$ among exact $((n, 2, \ge 3))$ codes whose full projective transversal group cannot be conjugated into the projective Clifford group.
summary: This paper provides a complete, finite classification of transversal diagonal gates acting on quantum error-correcting codes. By developing and applying the SSLP framework, the authors prove that the physical order of these gates is bounded by code parameters. This advances the understanding of quantum computation by characterizing non-Clifford logical symmetries in codes beyond the standard stabilizer framework.
main_problem: The paper aims to exhaustively classify transversal diagonal gates acting on exact qubit codes of distance at least two.
main_result: The classification is shown to be finite, and for $((6,2,3))$ codes, the method identifies 15 realizable symmetry classes supporting logical cyclic groups of orders 2, 3, and 5.
method: It employs the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework to separate discrete symmetry data from continuous code parameters, relying on the fact that the physical gate order is bounded by code parameters.
model_or_system: The system under study is abstract quantum error-correcting codes (qubit codes) defined by their parameters $((n, K, d))$, analyzed using the Knill–Laflamme conditions.
key_observables: Projective logical action, physical gate order, and the existence of specific transversal diagonal symmetries (e.g., cyclic groups $C_2, C_3, C_5$).
important_parameters: Code parameters $((n, K, d))$, the minimum length $n=6$ for certain non-Clifford supporting codes, and the order $q$ of the physical gate.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the projective logical action of a transversal diagonal gate can be realized by a physical gate of finite order, and this order is uniformly bounded by the code parameters.

paper_structure: The structure moves from establishing the finite nature of the classification, detailing the SSLP methodology, applying this to specific code parameters like $((6,2,3))$, and concluding with the unique classification of the order-five sector.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, systematic mathematical framework for classifying quantum gates beyond the standard stabilizer model, which is crucial for understanding the full computational power of quantum codes.
